<thought>The mass spectrum shows a classic carbon isotopic envelope: the M+1 peak is ~11 % of the monoisotopic peak, M+2 ~1 %, and each successive peak drops by roughly an order of magnitude. This pattern matches the natural ¹³C abundance and does not display the characteristic ~33 % (Cl) or ~100 % (Br) M+2 intensities, nor the ~4 % (S) M+2 intensity. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the observed isotope distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
